name: Greenput default — residential electrical (US)
disclaimer: EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS A PLACEHOLDER DEFAULT, NOT MARKET TRUTH. They are plausible 2026 US residential figures chosen so a new workspace produces a sane range on day one. Labour rates vary roughly 2x between metros, material prices move monthly, and permit fees are entirely jurisdictional. A contractor MUST tune these during setup; Greenput should treat an untuned rate card as a warning state on every quote it backs.

electrician_hourly.label: What do you charge for an hour of a licensed electrician's time?
electrician_hourly.note: Billed rate, not your cost. If you quote flat-rate off a book, enter the hourly this book implies for a 4-hour job.

helper_hourly.label: And for a helper or apprentice, when you bring one?

after_hours_multiplier.label: Evenings and nights are charged at

trip_charge.label: Do you charge to come out?

options.always: On every job, on top of the work
options.diagnostic_only: Only on diagnostic call-outs (rolled into the repair if they go ahead)
options.never: Never — it's built into my hourly

minimum_job.label: What is the smallest amount you will do a job for?
minimum_job.note: No machine may ever emit a low end below this.

emergency_callout.label: Same-day emergency call-out
emergency_callout.note: Shown as a disclosed rate on urgent terminals, never as a quote.

diagnostic_hours_included.label: How much time does a diagnostic call-out include?

markup_pct.label: How much do you add to parts?
markup_pct.note: Applied to your cost. Enter 0 if your hourly already covers parts margin.

sales_tax_pct.label: Sales tax you have to charge on materials
sales_tax_pct.note: Default 0 because taxability of contractor-installed materials differs by state and by whether you buy tax-paid. Set this deliberately or leave it at 0 and absorb it in markup.

breaker.2p_40a.label: 2-pole 40A breaker
breaker.2p_40a.note: Price varies 3x by panel brand. Square D QO and Eaton CH sit at the top; BR/Homeline at the bottom.

breaker.2p_50a_gfci.label: 2-pole 50A GFCI breaker
breaker.2p_50a_gfci.note: Required when a 14-50 receptacle feeds an EVSE (NEC 625.54). This single part is the most common reason a plug-in install prices above a hardwired one.

breaker.1p_20a_afci.label: 1-pole 20A AFCI / dual-function breaker
breaker.1p_20a_afci.note: The hidden cost of a panel replacement. Where the AHJ requires AFCI on reused circuits, a 20-circuit swap can carry $700-$1,000 of these.

device.recept_14_50.label: NEMA 14-50 receptacle, industrial grade
device.recept_14_50.note: The $14 residential part is the one that melts under 8 hours a night of EV charging. Spec the industrial one and say so on the quote.

mast.riser_kit_2in.label: 2" mast riser kit (weatherhead, straps, sill plate)

spd.type2_80ka.label: Type 2 surge protective device, ~80kA, longer warranty

spd.point_of_use.label: Point-of-use surge strip for sensitive electronics

evse.allowance_l2.label: Level 2 charger allowance (if we supply)
evse.allowance_l2.note: An ALLOWANCE, not a product. The quote must say which charger it assumes, or say plainly that the homeowner picks and any difference is passed through.

loadmgmt.evse_module.label: EV load-management / power-sharing module
loadmgmt.evse_module.note: The device that avoids a service upgrade on a tight 100A service. Often the honest cheaper answer.

options.we_pull_flat_fee: We pull it and charge a flat fee
options.we_pull_bill_actual: We pull it and pass the actual fee through
options.no_permit: We don't permit this kind of work

flat_fee.label: Your flat permit fee
flat_fee.note: Genuinely jurisdictional. An EV-charger permit is $60 in one town and $450 plus a stamped load calculation in the next. This is the single number most worth tuning per city you work in.

required_by_job_class.label: Which of these do you permit?

trench_lawn_per_ft.label: Trenching through lawn or soft dirt

trench_gravel_roots_per_ft.label: Trenching through gravel or heavy roots

concrete_cut_patch_per_ft.label: Cutting and patching concrete or asphalt
concrete_cut_patch_per_ft.note: Wide by nature. Where a run has to cross a slab, the machine should widen the band, not pretend to know.

utility_coordination_fee.label: Utility disconnect / reconnect fee you have to pay
utility_coordination_fee.note: Many utilities bill the homeowner directly. Default 0 and disclose it as a pass-through.

uncertainty.label: How sure do you want your ranges to be?

tight.blurb: Narrow ranges. You will occasionally eat a surprise to honour one.

comfortable.blurb: The default. Wide enough to absorb a normal bad day.

wide.blurb: Loose ranges. You will almost always come in under the top, which reads well — but a wide range converts worse.

uncertainty.flat_pad_cap_note: The flat pad never exceeds this share of the estimate. Without it a fixed dollar pad invents a huge percentage range on a small job — a $60 pad on a $420 surge protector is a 30% band conjured out of nothing, which is the opposite of honest.
uncertainty.skew_note: Fraction of the spread placed ABOVE the point estimate. 0.5 is symmetric. The default 0.6 reflects that electrical surprises are one-tailed: you find things behind walls, you never find fewer.
uncertainty.max_spread_note: Above this, the machine must stop quoting and book a visit. A range that wide is not information.

standard_exclusions: Patching and painting where we have to open a wall
Restoring lawn, landscaping or paving over a trench
Anything we find that is already unsafe and has to be fixed before we can connect
Utility company charges, if your utility bills you directly
Permit fees, if you choose to pull the permit yourself
presentation.range_promise: This is the price we will honour. If we get there and the job is genuinely different from what you described, we stop and talk to you before doing anything that costs more.

setup_wizard.title: Set your prices once
setup_wizard.intro: Answer six questions about how you charge. That's it — Greenput turns them into an instant price for every job type you switch on, and you can change any of them whenever you like.

steps.screen: What do you charge for an hour of your time?
steps.helper: Your billed rate for a licensed electrician. Not your cost.

steps.screen: Do you charge to come out?
steps.helper: Lots of electricians charge a call-out fee and waive it if the customer goes ahead. Say how you do it and we'll apply it the same way every time.

steps.screen: What's the smallest job you'll take?
steps.helper: No price we show will ever start below this.

steps.screen: How much do you add to parts?
steps.helper: We keep a parts list with normal prices. You can change any of them — most people change three or four and leave the rest.
If you pull them, tell us what you charge. Permit fees change from town to town, so it's worth setting this per area you work in.

steps.screen: How sure do you want your prices to be?
steps.helper: Homeowners see a range until you confirm the work order, then one exact number. You're committing to honour the range. A tighter range converts better and leaves you less room. Most people start Comfortable.

then.body: Switch on the jobs you want instant prices for. We'll show you exactly what a homeowner would be quoted for a typical version of each one, using your numbers — change anything that looks wrong.
then.preview_note: Every job type shows a worked example before you turn it on. You are never asked to trust a number you haven't seen produced.

setup_wizard.closing_note: You just built a pricing engine. It runs the same way every time, it shows its work, and nobody has to be at a desk for it to answer.
